title: softbodies
note: Artifact-level mind-map: every artifact placed heuristically from concept + tier + reading order. y = concept_order (timeline); x morphs from a single column (order) to concept clusters (x_spread).

concepts.key: A cube that won't hold its shape. Pres
concepts.truth: A cube that won't hold its shape. Press it, drop it, watch it recover — or not. The jelly cube is a spring-mass system: particles connected by elastic constraints, each one pulling its neighbors back toward rest.

concepts.key: Cloth hangs from a spinning carousel.
concepts.truth: Cloth hangs from a spinning carousel. Soft mushroom bodies dangle from arms, swinging outward as the ride turns — then slamming into obstacles. Walk through the straps. Feel them part around you.

concepts.key: Walls breathe. Flags dance. A trampoli
concepts.truth: Walls breathe. Flags dance. A trampoline catches what falls. Soft bodies don't just exist in space — they negotiate it. Every surface here pushes back, deforms, recovers, or doesn't.

concepts.key: Twelve more tests. Twelve more ways ma
concepts.truth: Twelve more tests. Twelve more ways matter refuses to behave.

concepts.key: A surface made of springs. Each vertex
concepts.truth: A surface made of springs. Each vertex connected to its neighbors by elastic constraints — stretch, shear, structural. The mesh holds shape not through rigidity but through thousands of tiny negotiations. Gravity pulls.

concepts.key: No instructions. No objectives. Just a
concepts.truth: No instructions. No objectives. Just a field of soft things waiting to be touched.

concepts.key: A single radiolarian floats in a displ
concepts.truth: A single radiolarian floats in a display case. One cell, no brain, no intention — yet its silica skeleton is geometry so precise that Ernst Haeckel drew it as art. Spikes radiate at computed angles.
Two chemicals. One miracle.

concepts.key: Matching pairs nodes. Given a graph, f
concepts.truth: Matching pairs nodes. Given a graph, find the largest set of edges where no vertex appears twice — every node matched at most once. In bipartite graphs this is straightforward.

concepts.key: The hopper bounces softly. Spring phys
concepts.truth: The hopper bounces softly. Spring physics. Deformable matter in deformable space. Everything gives when you push it.
